status: ORPHANED CAMPAIGN CONTENT, RETAINED AS A SIMULATOR FIXTURE. The episode this belonged to (episode-01-contact-unclassified) was deleted 2026-09-13 along with every other drafted beat beyond Session 0/1. This file survives ONLY because tools/battle-simulator/ground-layer/resolve-ground-layer.mjs and test/battle-simulator/ground-layer.test.mjs read its real DCs, and deleting it would break a tested tool. It is NOT current campaign content and must not be run at a table or built on. It is also built entirely on the five ground roles, which are themselves under review and may be removed - see open-questions.json#ground-roles-viability. If ground roles are cut, this file and the simulator layer that reads it both need a decision.
name: Day 1 — The Ground Layer
description: The five non-piloting kids, at street level, underneath a fight they cannot participate in. Runs in parallel with encounter day-1-the-fight, round for round, on the same three-round clock. Two things need doing and there is not enough time to do both — that shortfall is the entire design, and it is what sets the severity of scene 8.

thresholds.effect: Partial fix. The team can tell the pilot roughly where the weak point is. The Frame may Strike the Claimant, but the Interdiction Field still negates all damage — this threshold exists purely so the players can SEE they are getting somewhere, and so a Frame player has something to do in round 1 other than watch.

The field collapses. The Claimant is Stunned 2 and gains weakness 15 to all damage for the rest of the encounter. Announce this at the table as a call-out from a specific kid, by name — this is the moment the ground layer becomes load-bearing and it should be unmistakable.
Half clear. If the shelter is destroyed in scene 8, the losses are survivable and named — people the kids can visit afterwards.
Fully clear. If the shelter is destroyed in scene 8, they lose the PLACE and not the PEOPLE. This is the best available outcome; it is still a real loss, and scene 8 still happens.

dc.basis: level 1 standard DC — the kid's own level, never the Claimant's (data/campaign/ground-roles.json)

outcomes.criticalSuccess: 2 points. The kid sees it clearly and can describe it — let them describe it.
outcomes.failure: No progress. Describe what obscured it: smoke, angle, the sheer size of the thing.
outcomes.criticalFailure: No progress, and the kid is Exposed — they are caught in the open when the next collateral hazard triggers, taking a -2 circumstance penalty to that save.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: 2 points. Ask the player who specifically they got out, and write the name down. It will matter in scene 8 and afterwards.
outcomes.failure: No progress. People are frightened, slow, or refusing to leave without someone.
outcomes.criticalFailure: No progress, and the kid is Exposed as above.

obstacles.name: Collateral hazard (triggered by the Claimant's Advance)

dc.basis: level 2 hazard — deliberately one level above the kids, per the episode's 'real danger' requirement. Still nowhere near Frame-scale.

outcomes.criticalFailure: Double damage (avg 14) — roughly three-quarters of a level-1 kid's HP. A second one drops them.

obstacles.notes: Fires once per round, automatically, whenever the Claimant Advances — it is falling masonry, a ruptured main, a bus going through a shopfront. It is NOT the Claimant attacking: per its Scale-Blind ability it cannot perceive or target anyone at this scale. This is the only thing that threatens the ground team, and it is environmental, exactly as data/campaign/ground-roles.json requires ('Ground encounters use hazards and environment, never enemy statblocks').

participants.eligibility: Each of the five non-piloting kids. Any kid may attempt any obstacle they can justify — the five named Ground Roles suggest a natural fit but must not restrict choice, because the whole point of this scene is that they choose.
participants.actionsPerRound: One Spot OR one Shepherd per kid per round. The collateral hazard save is not an action and does not compete.

bounding.description: Three rounds, shared with encounter day-1-the-fight. 5 kids x 3 rounds = 15 actions total.
bounding.dynamicAdjustment: If the Frame's pilot goes berserk early (Bleed 10 before round 3), the ground layer ends immediately — there is nothing more to do but run. Kids still holding Shepherd progress lose any unbanked partial work.

winCondition: Field Integrity 6 AND Shelter Evacuation 8. This is not achievable — see notes. There is no 'win', only a choice about which loss.
rewards: Moderate accomplishment XP (30) to every kid regardless of outcome, per reference/tables/encounter-and-rewards-math.json — they were level-1 children under a Claimant and they stayed. Award it in scene 9, out loud, in the same flat institutional voice as the ratio.
notes:
THE MATH THAT MAKES THIS WORK. A level-1 kid, trained in a relevant skill with a +4 key attribute, has +7. Against DC 15 that is: critical success on a natural 18+ (15%), success on 8-17 (50%), failure on 2-7 (30%), critical failure on a natural 1 (5%). Expected yield per action = (0.15 x 2) + (0.50 x 1) = 0.8 points.

Five kids x three rounds = 15 actions = ~12 points expected. The two pools demand 6 + 8 = 14. THEY CANNOT DO BOTH. That two-point shortfall is deliberate and it is the whole scene: every action spent spotting the weak point is an action not spent getting people out of the shelter the berserking Frame is about to destroy, and every action spent on the shelter is an action that leaves the Frame swinging at an invulnerable target for another round.

Do not soften this by letting them do both. Do not have an NPC cover the gap. The trolley problem IS the session, and because it is generated by dice and player choice rather than authored, nobody at the table can accuse the GM of railroading them into it. Scene 8's severity is whatever they left undone — which means it is theirs, and they will remember it.
